text:
The unemployment rate is 10.0%, which matches October 2009. Fed funds is near 0.12%, and the 12-month equity return of +30% fits a window ending in early 2010 (March 2009 lows are still inside it).

Headline CPI at 2.82% YoY fits late 2009: October 2009 was +(-0.2)%, November 2009 was 1.8%, and December 2009 was 2.7%. A 3m change of +4.14 means CPI was about -1.3% three months earlier. July 2009 was -2.1% and August 2009 was -1.5%, so the latest is likely December 2009 (2.7%) or January 2010 (2.6%).

Unemployment was 10.0% in both October and December 2009, and 9.9% in January 2010. Core CPI at 1.79% suggests December 2009 (1.8%). The 10-year yield of 3.68% fits January 2010, though December 2009 was around 3.84%. The equity 1m return of -4.6% fits January 2010 (S&P -3.6%), and emerging markets at -7% also fits January. The 10-year yield rose 0.27 over 3 months, from about 3.4% in October, which is plausible. Gold was -1.4% in January 2010. The VIX at 23.7 also fits January 2010 (about 24.6).

Payrolls averaged -69k over the 3 months to January 2010 as revised. Unemployment may have been 10.0% on the vintage then available, so January 2010 is the best fit.
